gate: Gate R6 — Security & Privacy Release Audit Qualification
classification: FINLIFE RELEASE QUALIFICATION — GATE R6: SECURITY & PRIVACY AUDITED, CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY AUTHENTICATED, AND CERTIFIED AS A RELEASE-CANDIDATE BASELINE — FAIL-CLOSED WITHIN TESTED BOUNDARIES, NO OBSERVED SENSITIVE LOG LEAKAGE, AND THREAT-MODELED.

R6-SEC-01.description: Static code analysis: Zero hardcoded live API keys, private keys, or tokens in source files
R6-SEC-01.evidence: Scanned 558 source files across app/, services/, components/, constants/. Zero hardcoded credentials found.

R6-SEC-02.description: Production build configs and Gradle properties contain zero embedded plaintext signing secrets
R6-SEC-02.evidence: Gradle properties and build.gradle verified: Signing credentials injected via secure environment/keystore properties.

R6-SEC-03.description: Test fixtures and fault injections unconditionally rejected when NODE_ENV === "production"
R6-SEC-03.evidence: Production guards reject all debug/test fault injection hooks with FAULT_INJECTION_REJECTED.

R6-PERM-01.description: AndroidManifest.xml specifies android:allowBackup="false" to disable application backup participation
R6-PERM-01.evidence: Disables application backup participation for the release application and reduces unauthorized backup extraction exposure. Verified non-debuggable release configuration.

R6-PERM-02.description: Dangerous and unnecessary Android OS permissions pruned from AndroidManifest.xml
R6-PERM-02.evidence: Unnecessary high-risk permissions (Audio, Camera, External Storage, Alert Window, Location) pruned.

R6-PERM-03.evidence: SMS receiver explicitly protected with BROADCAST_SMS permission; rogue applications cannot spoof SMS broadcasts.

R6-PERM-04.description: Deep link schemes validated against open intent vulnerabilities with custom-scheme interception caveats
R6-PERM-04.evidence: Dangerous URI schemes are rejected and the approved custom scheme is validated; custom-scheme interception risk remains subject to Android intent and physical-device qualification.

R6-STOR-01.description: Financial persistence strictly confined to app-private internal sandbox
R6-STOR-01.evidence: StorageService operates strictly within app-private internal sandbox.

R6-STOR-02.description: Native Android codebase contains zero MODE_WORLD_READABLE or MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE references
R6-STOR-02.evidence: Zero world-accessible file mode flags found in native Android source tree.

R6-STOR-03.description: Strict DEMO vs PRODUCTION namespace and storage key isolation prevents cross-contamination
R6-STOR-03.evidence: Namespace isolation verified: DEMO (FINLIFE_CASHBOOK_DEMO_V1) and PROD (FINLIFE_CASHBOOK_PROD_V1) keys strictly partitioned.

R6-CRYPTO-01.description: Authenticated AES-256-GCM encryption enforced with 128-bit tag and 96-bit IV
R6-CRYPTO-01.evidence: AES-256-GCM verified: 96-bit randomized IV, 128-bit authentication tag, 128-bit random salt.

R6-CRYPTO-02.description: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 derivation benchmark meets required work factor (>= 100,000 iterations)
R6-CRYPTO-02.evidence: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 calibrated: 100,000 iterations completed in 44ms with 256-bit output.

R6-CRYPTO-03.description: Native FinlifeCryptoEngine implements StrongBox HSM with AndroidKeyStore TEE fallback
R6-CRYPTO-03.evidence: StrongBox is requested where supported, with Android Keystore/TEE fallback; actual hardware-backed capability is device-dependent. Verified native contract in FinlifeCryptoEngine.kt.

R6-CRYPTO-04.description: In-memory cryptographic hygiene: Mutable key material actively zeroed after use
R6-CRYPTO-04.evidence: Cryptographic key buffer memory hygiene verified: zeroed via fill(0) in export and restore.

R6-CRYPTO-05.description: Key rotation and re-encryption protocol: Changing passphrase re-encrypts with new salt, IV, and tag
R6-CRYPTO-05.evidence: Key rotation verified: New credentials generate distinct cryptographic material; old passphrase fails closed.

R6-LOG-01.description: services/secureLogger.js enforces allow-list logging and sanitizes payload structures
R6-LOG-01.evidence: Payload sanitization verified: allow-listed fields preserved while safeguarding object structures.

R6-LOG-02.description: Mandatory redaction: Passwords, PINs, CVVs, tokens, and keys always sanitized as [REDACTED]
R6-LOG-02.evidence: Sensitive credentials (password, pin, cvv, token, key, accountNumber) redacted as [REDACTED].

R6-LOG-03.description: Secondary regex masking sanitizes PAN cards, phone numbers, bearer tokens, bank accounts, and Aadhaar/UAN
R6-LOG-03.evidence: Regex masking verified: PAN cards, phone numbers, Bearer tokens, bank accounts, and Aadhaar/UAN sanitized.

R6-LOG-04.description: Production suppression: debug and info logging silenced in production environment
R6-LOG-04.evidence: Production suppression verified: secureLogger debug/info silenced when in production environment.

R6-LOG-05.description: Error normalization strips absolute file paths from stack traces
R6-LOG-05.evidence: Error normalization verified: local filesystem paths stripped and masked in stack snippets.

R6-INJ-01.description: Path traversal prevention: Backup and file operations reject "../" and absolute path injections
R6-INJ-01.evidence: Path traversal attempts (../, ..\, absolute paths) prevented via strict path.basename isolation.

R6-INJ-02.description: Prototype pollution defense: assertSafeObject rejects objects with __proto__, constructor, or prototype
R6-INJ-02.evidence: Prototype pollution defense verified: __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys throw SecurityError.

R6-INJ-03.description: Storage key injection prevention: Control characters and null bytes rejected in storage keys
R6-INJ-03.evidence: Storage key injection prevention verified: null bytes, newlines, and quotes fail closed.

R6-INJ-04.description: Monetary validation: Unsigned monetary inputs reject negative amounts; signed derived calculations permitted; malformed values fail closed
R6-INJ-04.evidence: Monetary boundary verified: Unsigned monetary inputs reject negative amounts; signed derived calculations permit negative BigInts; NaN, Infinity, and malformed strings rejected everywhere.

R6-DYN-01.description: Live Android logcat inspection: Zero unredacted credit cards, PINs, or raw balances logged by app
R6-DYN-01.evidence: Active logcat buffer inspected: Zero unredacted PANs, PINs, or plaintext passwords emitted.

R6-DYN-02.description: Process isolation verification: App executes under private sandboxed Linux UID on emulator-5554
R6-DYN-02.evidence: Sandboxed process verified: UID u0_a227, PID 23647 running in isolated Linux container.

R6-DYN-03.description: Cryptographic tamper rejection: Single bit flip in ciphertext fails closed with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED
R6-DYN-03.evidence: Tamper resistance verified: 1-bit ciphertext modification triggers AUTHENTICATION_TAG_VERIFICATION_FAILED.

R6-THREAT-01.description: Threat model boundaries explicitly separate protected defenses from kernel/hardware compromise
R6-THREAT-01.evidence: Formal Threat Model boundaries declared: 5 in-scope mitigations documented with qualified transport security; 3 out-of-scope boundaries documented.

environmentScope.boundary: Automated emulator qualification verified. Physical Android devices, OEM-specific behavior, and hardware penetration testing remain pending in subsequent gates.
